learn.rule: A complete sentence is a whole idea. It names who or what and tells what happens.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración completa es una idea entera. Dice quién o qué y lo que sucede.
learn.model: Sea otters wrap themselves in kelp while they sleep.
learn.notice: Find the who (sea otters) and what happens (wrap themselves in kelp). Together they make a whole idea.

items.prompt: Which group of words about sea otters is a complete sentence?

options.text: Floating near the surface of the kelp forest.
Sea otters wrap themselves in kelp so they do not drift away.
Because the kelp keeps the pups close to their mothers.

items.why: A complete sentence names who or what and tells what happens. Only this choice has both parts.
items.whyEs: Una oración completa dice quién o qué y lo que sucede. Solo esta opción tiene las dos partes.

items.prompt: What is missing from this fragment about a deep-sea animal?
items.text: Lives in the cold, dark water far below the surface.

options.text: a period at the end
the who or what the sentence is about
a describing word

items.why: Lives tells what happens, but we do not know who lives there. A sentence needs a who or what.
items.whyEs: Lives dice lo que sucede, pero no sabemos quién vive allí. Una oración necesita un quién o un qué.

items.prompt: Choose the word that gives this octopus sentence its action.
parts: through very small gaps between the rocks.
items.model: Octopuses squeeze through very small gaps between the rocks.
items.why: Squeeze is the action word. Now the sentence tells who and what happens, so it is a whole idea.
items.whyEs: Squeeze es la palabra de acción. Ahora la oración dice quién y qué sucede, así que es una idea completa.

items.prompt: What kind of group of words is this one about coral reefs?
items.text: Coral reefs grow in warm water many fish live there.

options.text: fragment
complete sentence
run-on

items.why: Two whole ideas are stuck together with no break. That is a run-on. A period or a joining word fixes it.
items.whyEs: Dos ideas completas están pegadas sin pausa. Eso es una oración sin pausa (run-on). Un punto o una palabra de unión lo arregla.

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about life in the sea.

options.text: The tide pulling the water higher up the beach.
Dolphins find fish by sending out clicking sounds.
Washed up on the sand after the storm.
A jellyfish has no brain, bones, or heart.
Whales sing songs that travel for miles underwater.

items.why: A complete sentence has a who or what and an action. The two fragments leave out one of those parts.
items.whyEs: Una oración completa tiene un quién o qué y una acción. Los dos fragmentos dejan fuera una de esas partes.

items.prompt: Which choice fixes the run-on about dolphins?
items.text: Dolphins click underwater the sounds bounce off fish and return to them.

options.text: Dolphins click underwater, the sounds bounce off fish and return to them.
Dolphins click underwater the sounds. Bounce off fish and return to them.
Dolphins click underwater. The sounds bounce off fish and return to them.

items.why: Each whole idea gets its own sentence with a capital letter and a period. A comma alone cannot join two sentences.
items.whyEs: Cada idea completa tiene su propia oración con mayúscula y punto. Una coma sola no puede unir dos oraciones.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about an ocean animal. Tell who or what it is and what it does.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre un animal del océano. Di quién o qué es y qué hace.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula

write.model: Sea turtles swim thousands of miles to lay their eggs on the beach.

familyTalk.en: At dinner, each person says one whole idea about an animal. Ask: 'Who is it about? What happens?'
familyTalk.es: En la cena, cada persona dice una idea completa sobre un animal. Pregunten: '¿De quién o de qué trata? ¿Qué sucede?'

teacherTip.en: Have students clap the who and the what-happens in each model sentence before they decide whether a group of words is complete.
teacherTip.es: Pide que los estudiantes marquen con palmadas el quién y el qué sucede en cada oración modelo antes de decidir si un grupo de palabras está completo.

learn.rule: A sentence needs a who or what and an action. A fragment is missing one. A run-on joins two ideas with no break.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración necesita un quién o qué y una acción. Un fragmento deja fuera una. Una oración sin pausa (run-on) une dos ideas sin pausa.
learn.model: The Nile River flooded every year and left rich soil on its banks.
learn.notice: Who or what? The Nile River. What happened? It flooded and left rich soil.

items.prompt: Which words about ancient Egypt make a complete sentence?

options.text: Growing wheat and barley along the river.
Where the farmers planted wheat and barley.
Farmers along the Nile grew wheat and barley.

items.why: Farmers is the who and grew is what happened. The other two groups leave an idea unfinished.
items.whyEs: Farmers es el quién y grew es lo que sucedió. Los otros dos grupos dejan una idea sin terminar.

items.prompt: What does this fragment about the pyramids need?
items.text: The tall stone pyramids near the river.

options.text: a verb that tells what the pyramids did or were
a capital letter
a different end mark

items.why: We know what the sentence is about, but not what happens. Adding stand or were built makes it a whole idea.
items.whyEs: Sabemos de qué trata la oración, pero no lo que sucede. Agregar stand o were built la convierte en una idea completa.

items.prompt: Choose the words that make this scribe sentence complete.
parts: on sheets made from papyrus plants.
items.model: Egyptian scribes wrote on sheets made from papyrus plants.
items.why: A sentence needs a verb that works as the action. Wrote is the action. Writing and who wrote leave the idea unfinished.
items.whyEs: Una oración necesita un verbo que sea la acción. Wrote es la acción. Writing y who wrote dejan la idea sin terminar.

items.prompt: What kind of group of words is this one about river boats?
items.text: Boats carried grain down the river merchants sold it in the markets.

options.text: fragment
run-on
complete sentence

items.why: There are two whole ideas with no break between them. That makes it a run-on.
items.whyEs: Hay dos ideas completas sin pausa entre ellas. Eso la hace una oración sin pausa (run-on).

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about life near the Nile.

options.text: Egyptians built boats from bundles of reeds.
Because the river brought water to the dry land.
Many families lived in villages close to the water.
The farmers who planted seeds after the flood.
Children helped carry baskets to the fields.

items.why: Complete sentences tell who and what happens. A group that starts with because or who often needs more to be finished.
items.whyEs: Las oraciones completas dicen quién y qué sucede. Un grupo que empieza con because o who muchas veces necesita más para terminar.

items.prompt: Which choice fixes the run-on about the flood?
items.text: The river rose in summer the fields were covered with water.

options.text: The river rose in summer, the fields were covered with water.
The river rose in summer the fields. Were covered with water.
The river rose in summer. The fields were covered with water.

items.why: Split the two ideas into two sentences. A comma by itself is not strong enough to join them.
items.whyEs: Separa las dos ideas en dos oraciones. Una coma sola no es suficiente para unirlas.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about how people used the Nile River.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre cómo usaba la gente el río Nilo.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula

write.model: Ancient Egyptians used the Nile to water crops, travel by boat, and move heavy stones.

familyTalk.en: Ask someone at home: 'What does our family use water for?' Answer in one whole idea.
familyTalk.es: Pregunten en casa: '¿Para qué usa agua nuestra familia?' Respondan con una idea completa.

teacherTip.en: Write one fragment and one run-on from today's reading on the board and let pairs repair each one aloud.
teacherTip.es: Escribe en la pizarra un fragmento y una oración sin pausa (run-on) de la lectura de hoy y deja que las parejas reparen cada uno en voz alta.

learn.rule: A complete sentence has a who or what and an action. Check for both, and check that two ideas are not stuck together.
learn.ruleEs: Una oración completa tiene un quién o qué y una acción. Revisa que estén las dos y que no haya dos ideas pegadas.
learn.model: A denominator tells how many equal parts make up the whole.
learn.notice: Who or what? A denominator. What does it do? It tells how many equal parts make the whole.

items.prompt: Which words about fractions make a complete sentence?

options.text: Two out of eight equal parts of the pizza.
Two-eighths of the pizza is covered with mushrooms.
Covered with mushrooms and extra cheese.

items.why: Two-eighths of the pizza is the who or what, and is covered with mushrooms is what happens.
items.whyEs: Two-eighths of the pizza es el quién o qué, y is covered with mushrooms es lo que sucede.

items.prompt: What does this fragment about a number line need?
items.text: The point halfway between zero and one.

options.text: a different end mark
a capital letter at the start
a verb that tells what the point is or does

items.why: The group already has a capital letter and a period. It names a thing but never says what the point is or does.
items.whyEs: El grupo ya tiene mayúscula y punto. Nombra algo, pero nunca dice qué es o qué hace el punto.

items.prompt: Choose the word that completes this sentence about denominators.
parts: how many equal parts make the whole.
items.model: A denominator tells how many equal parts make the whole.
items.why: Tells is the verb that finishes the idea. Telling and that tells leave the sentence hanging.
items.whyEs: Tells es el verbo que termina la idea. Telling y that tells dejan la oración sin terminar.

items.prompt: What kind of group of words is this one about halves and thirds?
items.text: Half of twelve is six a third of twelve is four.

options.text: fragment
complete sentence
run-on

items.why: Two complete ideas run together with no punctuation. Put a period between them to fix the run-on.
items.whyEs: Dos ideas completas van juntas sin puntuación. Pon un punto entre ellas para arreglar la oración sin pausa (run-on).

items.prompt: Check every complete sentence about measuring shapes.

options.text: The length of the rectangle times its width.
Perimeter is the distance around a shape.
Measuring with a ruler marked in eighths of an inch.
Area counts the square units inside a shape.
A square has four equal sides.

items.why: Each complete sentence has a who or what and an action. The two fragments name things but never say what happens.
items.whyEs: Cada oración completa tiene un quién o qué y una acción. Los dos fragmentos nombran cosas pero nunca dicen qué sucede.

items.prompt: Which choice fixes this run-on about a rectangle?
items.text: A rectangle has four sides opposite sides are equal in length.

options.text: A rectangle has four sides, opposite sides are equal in length.
A rectangle has four sides. Opposite sides are equal in length.
A rectangle has four sides opposite. Sides are equal in length.

items.why: Break the two ideas apart at the right spot. The first idea ends after sides.
items.whyEs: Separa las dos ideas en el lugar correcto. La primera idea termina después de sides.

write.prompt: Write one complete sentence about a shape or a fraction you know.
write.promptEs: Escribe una oración completa sobre una figura o una fracción que conozcas.

label: I started with a capital letter
Empecé con mayúscula

write.model: A fraction such as three-fourths shows three of four equal parts.

familyTalk.en: Find a shape at home, such as a plate or a window. Say one whole idea about it.
familyTalk.es: Busquen una figura en casa, como un plato o una ventana. Digan una idea completa sobre ella.

teacherTip.en: Ask students to underline the verb in each complete sentence; a group of words with no verb is a fragment.
teacherTip.es: Pide que los estudiantes subrayen el verbo en cada oración completa; un grupo de palabras sin verbo es un fragmento.
